english: Here $\log_{e}$ denotes the natural logarithm. The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\left(e^{x}-1\right)\log_{e}(1+x)-x^{2}}{x^{4}}$ is
hindi: यहाँ $\log_{e}$ प्राकृतिक लघुगणक को दर्शाता है। $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\left(e^{x}-1\right)\log_{e}(1+x)-x^{2}}{x^{4}}$ का मान है
solution: The $x^{3}$ term vanishes, so the limit is the $x^{4}$ coefficient $\dfrac{1}{4}$
solution_full: So the numerator is $\dfrac{x^{4}}{4}+O(x^{5})$, and the limit is $\dfrac{1}{4}$.
(Stopping at the $x^{3}$ term would wrongly suggest the limit $0$, option (C); the series must be carried to the fourth order.)
originality_note: New: the product (e^x - 1) log(1+x) has its x^3 term cancel, so the limit needs the fourth-order coefficients of both series (way 4, a hidden cancellation). Closest known: limits such as (e^x - 1 - x)/x^2 or log(1+x) series limits. Different because: the cancellation of the x^3 term forces a fourth-order product.

concept_use.Exponential and logarithmic series (e^x,: The series of e^x - 1 and log(1+x) up to x^3 are multiplied to get the x^4 coefficient 1/4.
concept_use.Evaluation of limit using expansion: The limit is evaluated by reading the leading coefficient of the expansion of the numerator over x^4.

stem_review: Read as a student: log_e defined, the limit is a single expression with no parameters; answer 1/4 at option B as planned; options numbers; Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: Multiply the two series to fourth order and notice the x^3 term cancels.
justification: Routine series multiplication carried one order further than usual; several standard steps, no insight. Close to 2025-P2-Q1 (L2, a limit by expansion).
